source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Having fairly little measurable effect on any type of heparin-based anticoagulant product a client might happen to be given during treatment","B":"A medication generally considered inappropriate for use alongside any heparin-based anticoagulant product whatsoever, in most clinical situations","C":"Reversing enoxaparin's anticoagulant effect to much the same complete degree that it reverses unfractionated heparin therapy given intravenously","D":"Only partially reverses the anticoagulant effect of low molecular weight heparins like enoxaparin, unlike its more complete reversal of unfractionated heparin"}}
source_row.rationale: Protamine sulfate only partially reverses the anticoagulant effect of low molecular weight heparins such as enoxaparin, in contrast to its more complete reversal of unfractionated heparin.
source_row.source_detail: Partial Reversal of LMWH vs. Complete Reversal of Unfractionated Heparin
